The rail starts below toolbar/top spacing (68dp) on apps, keeping controls reachable on short windows and both rail sides.

List picker/editor headers remain outside inner scrolling content. Android source and screenshots are authoritative.

components.name: Alphabet rail
components.description: Illustrative native translation. Bottom-aligned compact column with a 22dp letter step that grows with system font scale and 24dp clearance above system navigation; only favorites ordering reserves its temporary Done footer. Resting letters are 16sp and grow by up to 7sp near the finger, capped to the available step in short windows. Every window shows only A–Z and # sections with visible apps plus the star for home navigation. Hiding the last visible app immediately removes its section; undo and showing again restore it. Cyrillic initials use the first Latin letter of Android ICU Russian-Latin/BGN transliteration, including Яндекс → Yandeks → Y; numbers, symbols and initials without Latin transliteration use #. Below the letters, an active release selects the final section even without a final MOVE; cancelled gestures stay cancelled. Section changes and active releases use the same native CLOCK_TICK; each release emits exactly one tick even on the same section or when committing the final hash. Cancelled and inactive releases stay quiet, respecting Android haptic settings. Runtime is one continuous accessible control with finger-following Canvas geometry, not individual letter buttons.
components.html: ★CDFMP#
components.css: .ds-rail-stage { background:#352E2A; padding:16px; } .ds-rail { width:92px; min-height:448px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:flex-end; padding:24px 0; color:#FFFFFFE6; cursor:ns-resize; } .ds-rail span { display:block; width:48px; margin-left:36px; text-align:center; min-height:22px; font:500 16px sans-serif; } .ds-rail .ds-rail-selected { color:#FFFFFF; } .ds-rail:hover .ds-rail-selected, .ds-rail:focus-visible .ds-rail-selected, .ds-rail:active .ds-rail-selected { transform:translateX(-24px); font-size:23px; } .ds-rail:focus-visible { outline:none; }

components.name: App management sheet
components.description: Native long-press menu: #031629 surface, #BCD7F3 text and contour icons, rounded 24dp top corners, installed app icon and tappable 48dp-minimum title with accessible rename action, growing 17sp action rows with 48dp icon slots and 16dp gap, flat action list with favorites and favorite ordering first, then hide for visible apps, uninstall and app details; notifications/quick actions and attached-app selection remain in the icon-hold pop-up with its Add apps action, no Additional/expansion row and no rename row; hidden search results expose Show again directly with an open-eye contour icon and retain the current query/results after showing again, divider and Better Launcher settings. System insets and 85% display-height scroll cap. Native 300ms decelerating rise (0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) after settled insets/window layout, native window dimming and 180ms exit, and system animation scaling. Source: MainActivity.showAppMenu and anim/app_menu_*; this metadata does not replace native rendering. Inline rename replaces commands in the same sheet, uses a right-aligned Save and reserves IME space inside a fixed transparent window.

components.name: Widget provider picker
components.description: Native provider picker: no redundant visible title or Close; one tonal search toolbar with magnifier and contextual Clear, recycled list with wrapping 18sp widget label, 13sp app name and 144dp inert preview. Static previewLayout takes precedence over previewImage; missing previews are explicitly labeled. Shared 92dp AlphabetRail on the right, 72dp list reservation, star jumps to start, final # only when populated, populated sections at every height, with spacing adapting to font scale and available height. Background resource loading is cancelled on row reuse and dismissal. No IDs are allocated while browsing. Android source is authoritative; no HTML sample substitutes for device verification. Shared navy menu: #031629 surface, #BCD7F3 text/icons, 24dp top corners, 12dp/24dp/16dp padding plus system/IME insets; common 300ms arrival and fixed transparent window. The search toolbar stays outside the scrolling results. List labels and alphabet use the shared pale blue foreground; provider previews keep their own rendering.

components.name: Widget edge editor
components.description: Native editor over the real hosted AppWidgetHostView. Four 36dp circular navy handles inside 48dp touch targets carry pale blue paired chevrons; 2dp navy lines track bounds. There are no circular reset arrows. A bottom strip outside system bars shows live width × height and Done, with an 8dp gap from handle touch bounds. Supported axes/min/max come from the provider; width resizes around its saved center and upper-edge changes preserve the lower edge through a local top offset. Drag the body to move both axes, snapping to a 12dp grid inside the content column and above the editor strip. Keyboard arrows and named accessibility actions also move the body. Edited dimensions snap to the same grid within provider constraints. Mouse/touch cancellation restores the gesture snapshot; keyboard arrows and accessibility range actions edit the same dimensions. Done, outside tap, Back/HOME and lifecycle cleanup finish; ordinary provider touches work outside editing. The navy management menu uses a four-direction arrow icon for moving/resizing and omits reset and transfer from home to the widget page; page widgets retain placement on home. The widget menu omits “App info” and “Add widget” on both home and the widget page. Adding remains available by holding free space on the widget page and from the home-widget settings row; provider app details remain in the app long-press menu. Android screenshots are authoritative; no HTML mock is used. The home widget has a separate full inset-safe-width region, starts immediately at the inset-safe top with zero additional padding, and defaults to centered width with approximately 36dp side margins plus provider padding. Home width can expand beneath the alphabet to the exact window edge between grid points, subject to provider limits; page widgets retain 28dp column margins. Every applied width/height change requests one native CLOCK_TICK on all supported Android versions, including keyboard and accessibility input. The platform API exposes no amplitude parameter for CLOCK_TICK; strength follows the device implementation and system haptic settings. Repeated snapped dimensions, provider/window limits, movement without resizing, release without a new size and cancellation add no tick. Android haptic settings remain respected. The complete 48dp top-handle touch target stays below system bars/cutouts by moving inside the widget when necessary; this adds no widget layout padding.

narrative.overview:
The user selected Niagara's vertical favorites and alphabetical navigation. The current implementation expresses that direction through native Android Views: an open wallpaper surface, white app names, installed app icons, a continuous alphabet control, and dark native sheets. Better Launcher uses original Kotlin source under its own product name and displays the system wallpaper.

Settings and all app-owned menus use a navy and pale blue Material 3 theme, while the launcher itself stays visually open. This document describes the implemented phone UI, not verified Niagara fidelity or full feature parity. The native source is authoritative: [MainActivity.kt](app/src/main/java/app/better/launcher/MainActivity.kt), [LauncherViews.kt](app/src/main/java/app/better/launcher/LauncherViews.kt), and [styles.xml](app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml). Review captures are stored locally in `.impeccable/review/`; the historical five material corrections for 0.1.0 have a scoped `ship` verdict in [verification.md](docs/verification.md).
keyCharacteristics: Unboxed installed app rows over system wallpaper.
All app-owned menus and settings use navy surfaces, pale blue labels and contour icons.
Shared inset-aware sheets, growing rows, native controls and stable bottom anchoring.
Continuous alphabet with keyboard and accessibility alternatives.

rules.name: The Readable Wallpaper Rule
rules.body: A native Material slider controls black scrim opacity from 0% (fully visible wallpaper) to 100% (black background), in 1% steps. The default is 20%, with no mandatory contrast floor. The inline percentage updates and saves immediately; the slider supports keyboard and accessibility input. Lower dimming can reduce white-text contrast on bright wallpapers. Legacy enabled dimming maps to 20%, disabled dimming to 0%; an explicitly saved percentage takes precedence.

rules.name: The Grow With Text Rule
rules.body: App and settings rows use minimum heights, not fixed text containers; preserve wrapping when Android font scale grows. The temporary Done footer remains outside scrolling content only during favorites ordering. App results use a native ListView that recycles visible rows with content-driven heights.

rules.name: The Full Home Height Rule
rules.body: Normal home fills the inset-safe height without bottom search/widget/settings buttons or a 66dp footer reserve. Swipe up on free space opens search, swipe right opens widgets, and holding free space opens settings. Search and Menu/Shift+F10 provide keyboard entry; the home accessibility node exposes all three named actions. Only ordering has a separate temporary Done footer.

rules.name: The Open List Rule
rules.body: Keep launcher app rows unboxed at rest and throughout favorites and widget dragging; widget providers retain their own backgrounds; reserve opaque containers for sheets, settings, notification detail, and transient feedback, as the current build does.

rules.name: Widget picker search
rules.body: The provider picker omits its visible heading and separate Close. A single tonal #112B42 search field has a leading contour magnifier, 17sp pale blue text/hint, growing 56dp minimum height and 16dp corners. Its trailing 48dp Clear appears only for nonempty input; space is reserved to prevent shifts. Pane title remains accessible; Back/outside taps dismiss and HOME returns home. A background-prepared index matches widget/application names without case/diacritic sensitivity. Results reset to the top and determine the right alphabet; no matches hides the rail and gives accessible recovery guidance. Keyboard opens on tap; IME Done hides it, with standard system input in landscape. Browsing/search never allocates IDs.

rules.name: The Separate Widget Page Rule
rules.body: Home hosts at most one widget. The separate wallpaper-backed page to its left opens with a rightward swipe on home, including app and folder rows, or settings and the named home accessibility action and returns with a leftward swipe or Android Back. Hosted widgets and ordering handles keep their gestures; the outer 24dp Back edge is reserved. The widget page uses the wallpaper and occupies the complete inset-safe height, with no visible title, Back/Add/reorder toolbar, Home footer or extra vertical padding. Widgets retain 28dp side margins and the saved widget spacing. Holding empty wallpaper, a list gap or side margin opens the provider picker directly; the fill-viewport content keeps unused space touchable even on an empty or short page. The empty page only explains the hold gesture. A named accessibility long-click action and Menu/Shift+F10 on focused free space offer adding without a visible control. System Back and a leftward swipe return home. Ordering starts from the widget management menu for two or more widgets; Back ends ordering, and HOME returns normal home. The actual hosted views remain visible and receiving updates, with a single 48dp drag handle below each widget with keyboard/accessibility moves. Dropping or keyboard/accessibility moves save; cancel restores positions. Edge scrolling reaches long lists. Back finishes; HOME returns normal home. Duplicate instances use ordinal accessibility labels. Home ID, host bindings, sizes and offsets remain attached to the widget. Long press opens order, resize, optional provider configuration, move and delete. Four native 48dp edge handles edit live width/height directly with navy 2dp boundary lines. No circular reset buttons or slider sheet appear. Sizes and top offset save locally; provider directions/min/max and window bounds apply. Keyboard/range actions resize the same edges; Done, outside tap, Back/HOME finish. The navy management menu uses a four-direction arrow icon for moving/resizing and omits reset and transfer from home to the widget page; page widgets retain placement on home. The widget menu omits “App info” and “Add widget” on both home and the widget page. Adding remains available by holding free space on the widget page and from the home-widget settings row; provider app details remain in the app long-press menu. Narrower widgets start centered and can move inside their content column with saved horizontal/top offsets on a 12dp grid. Provider taps/scrolling remain available, with Menu/Shift+F10 and accessibility long-click alternatives. A 180ms directional slide/fade honors disabled system animations. The alphabet reserves system/IME insets and only the currently visible ordering footer height; normal home and apps share the same bottom anchor.

rules.name: The Favorites Order Rule
rules.body: Favorites enter ordering from the long-press app menu, with no duplicate button below favorites. They reorder on home with a single 48dp handle at the trailing edge of each title line, vertically centered with the app/folder name, including wrapped labels. No separate button line or visible up/down buttons. Keyboard arrows and valid named accessibility moves belong to the handle; boundary actions are omitted. Preserve alphabet margins, Back corridor, full IDs, edge scrolling, save on drop, cancellation, fixed Done and Back/HOME exit.

rules.name: App pop-up actions
rules.body: The app pop-up contains notifications, shortcuts, attached apps and “Add apps”. It has no “Open …” action for its owner; tapping the original app row launches it.

dos: **Do** preserve the user's Niagara-style vertical lists and alphabetical navigation.
**Do** keep app rows transparent and use installed app icons and actual system data.
**Do** respect the selected wallpaper dimming percentage and use pale blue secondary text.
**Do** use the full inset-safe home height and keep the temporary ordering Done outside scrolling content.
**Do** let text rows grow with font scale and preserve keyboard and accessibility alternatives.
**Do** use native Material 3 controls within the existing dark theme.
donts: **Don't** replace the selected launcher composition with a card grid or a new brand metaphor.
**Don't** copy the raw ripple-mask radius as a density-aware spacing or shape token.
**Don't** treat panel CSS samples or synthesized tonal ramps as Android source values.
**Don't** claim exact Niagara fidelity, full feature parity, tablet support, or physical-device validation from this phone build.
